rfm_tuples.R: 10-K FY2023 (Aug 2023): 'We expect to refinance the MSG Networks Credit Facilities prior to their maturity in October 2024, including paying down a portion of the MSG Networks' term loan in connection therewith.' Reframed in Q3 FY24 10-Q (May 10, 2024) — only 5 months before maturity — as: 'While this condition raises substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern... we have concluded this condition has been effectively alleviated' (management self-assessment, NOT auditor; this is interim, unaudited).
rfm_tuples.f: Claim-evolution: compare 10-K refinancing-confidence vs Q1-Q3 FY24 going-concern language. Cross-check covenant ratios disclosed in MSGN Credit Agreement note.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Going-concern / substantial-doubt language FIRST APPEARS in Q1 FY24 10-Q (Nov 8, 2023), driven by London Sphere cancellation (Nov 21, 2023 announced) + Q2 $115.7M impairment, NOT in the 10-K. 870.4M term loan reclassified short-term. As of 2024-05-10, no executed refinancing announced, just MOU/expectation language.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 10-K (Aug 2023) presented refinancing as routine; within 3 months going-concern language emerged. The refinancing was still 'expected' but unconsummated 5 days before cutoff. Management's claim that substantial doubt is 'effectively alleviated' rests on a sentence-stuffed argument about non-recourse to Non-Credit Parties — sophisticated but a structural admission that the MSGN Holdings stack could fail. Material disclosure-evolution signal.

rfm_tuples.R: MSGN Credit Agreement: 'requires the MSGN Holdings Entities... to comply with a maximum total leverage ratio of 5.50:1.00... As of March 31, 2024, the total leverage ratio was 5.36:1.00... a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.00:1.00... As of March 31, 2024, the interest coverage ratio was 2.24:1.00.'
rfm_tuples.f: Covenant-cushion deterioration trend: pull ratios from each pre-cutoff 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Leverage: Q1 5.27 -> Q2 5.29 -> Q3 5.36 (vs 5.50 max, only 2.5% cushion at Q3). Interest coverage: Q1 2.50 -> Q2 2.47 -> Q3 2.24 (vs 2.00 min, only 12% cushion at Q3). MSG Networks affiliation revenue declined $49.3M FY22->FY23 due to subscriber attrition + Comcast non-renewal (Sept 2021); 9mo FY24 media revenue $407.6M vs $442.8M PY = -8% YoY. Both covenants trending toward breach with no apparent reversal driver.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: MSGN covenant cushion is thin and deteriorating, driven by secular RSN decline (cord-cutting, sports rights inflation). Without refinancing or covenant amendment, breach within 1-2 quarters is plausible. Mode-B finding: 10-K narrative treated MSGN as a stable cash cow; Q-disclosures show it's actually the LIABILITY that triggered going concern.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (Aug 2023): 'In February 2018, we announced the purchase of land in Stratford, London... we have announced plans to build another Sphere venue, pending necessary approvals.' Q3 FY24 (May 2024): 'On November 21, 2023, we announced that we were formally notified by the Mayor of London that our planning application for a Sphere venue in Stratford, London was not approved... no longer plans to allocate resources towards the development.'
rfm_tuples.f: Track impairment recognition vs 10-K disclosed risk language. Cross-check capex assets retired.
rfm_tuples.M_value: $115.7M impairment recognized Q2 FY24 (Dec 2023 quarter) on construction-in-progress and land in Sphere segment, driven by London non-approval. 10-K had treated London approval as 'pending necessary approvals' (forward-looking, but not flagged as elevated risk). Result: 9mo FY24 operating loss $269.9M vs $202.7M PY.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: London cancellation was a discrete government decision and 10-K disclosure was honest (not concealed) — but the company's expansion thesis materially impaired between 10-K and cutoff. Material adverse change consistent with the drawdown.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (Aug 2023): Auditor 'Deloitte & Touche LLP' (Big 4); FY22 material weakness identified and 'has been remediated' as of June 30, 2022; ICFR opinion clean in FY23.
rfm_tuples.f: Auditor identity + ICFR opinion + history of material weakness.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Deloitte (Big 4, tier-1). FY21-Q3FY22 material weakness in spinoff-related controls, remediated by Q4 FY22. No new material weakness in FY23 or Q1-Q3 FY24. No auditor resignation or disagreement disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Audit quality is strong. Prior material weakness was complexity-driven (multiple spinoffs from MSG Sports lineage) not aggressive accounting. Reduces probability that disclosed numbers are misstated.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied claim (10-K + Q-comms): Sphere Las Vegas — opened Sept 2023 with U2 residency, then Postcard from Earth (immersive). Management thesis: Sphere LV will generate cash to service convertible notes + LV Sphere Term Loan + support MSGN refinancing.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify Sphere segment financial trajectory across first 3 quarters post-opening; pull insider behavior as best-evidence of management conviction.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Sphere segment: Q3 FY24 rev $170.4M (vs $0.6M PY), 9mo rev $345.9M, but 9mo Sphere segment operating loss $269.9M (incl $115.7M London impairment, plus heavy D&A from CIP coming online, $19M restructuring). Cash position: unrestricted cash $680.6M at March 31, 2024 vs $131.9M at June 30, 2023 — recovered via $258.8M 3.50% Convertible Notes (Dec 2023) AND positive Sphere ticket-revenue + advance ticket proceeds ($125M of cash is advance ticket proceeds). INSIDER signal: CEO/Executive Chair James L. Dolan executed OPEN-MARKET PURCHASES (Form 4 code P) of approximately 245,669 shares across Feb 26 - Mar 4, 2024 at prices $40.70 - $47.60 (rough notional ~$10.6M), AFTER the going-concern language and London impairment. Other insiders: routine RSU vests (M) and tax-withholding (F), plus 2 small open-market sales (Greenberg, Byrnes - aggregate immaterial).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Sphere LV is generating real venue revenue ($170M/qtr), proving the venue works, but segment economics are not yet self-sustaining. CEO open-market purchases ~$10M after going-concern disclosure is a STRONG positive insider signal — most fraudulent or doomed companies see insider selling, not buying, during distress periods. Dolan's purchase price ($40-48) is the floor he's defending. This materially weakens a SHORT-tier thesis.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K + 10-Qs: MSG Networks 'Substantially all of our affiliation fee revenue comes from our top four Distributors' — top 4 = unnamed but historically Comcast, Charter/Spectrum, Altice, Verizon/AT&T. Comcast carriage NOT renewed at Sept 2021 expiry.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A: verify concentration disclosure; Mode-B: derive what isn't said (which 4? identification masking).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Top 4 Distributor concentration is disclosed but the identities of the four distributors are NOT named, only adverse Comcast non-renewal. With Comcast already gone, the top 4 today must include Charter/Spectrum, Altice, Verizon, DirecTV/AT&T, Cox or similar. Each renewal cycle = binary cliff risk. 9mo FY24 affiliation -8% YoY consistent with ongoing subscriber declines + possible smaller renewal repricings.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B: a clean disclosure would name each top distributor and quantify % concentration per Item 101. Sphere/MSGN obscures identities and exact %, which is allowable but reduces investor ability to model cliff dates. Not a lie, but information-asymmetric.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'Class B common stock... 6,866,754 shares' + 'certain members of the Dolan family... collectively beneficially owned 100% of the Company's outstanding Class B common stock.'
rfm_tuples.f: Governance verification: confirm Class A vs Class B voting structure and Dolan control.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Dual-class with Dolan Family 100% of Class B (high vote/share), 6.87M Class B shares vs ~35M Class A. Confirmed in Q3 FY24 Note 15. Dolan-affiliated related-party transactions disclosed (cross-services with MSGS, MSGE).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Controlled company structure is well-disclosed and consistent across filings. Reduces risk of governance surprise but increases minority-shareholder dependence on Dolan judgment. James Dolan's open-market buying (C5) is most powerful when paired with this — he is the controlling shareholder buying alongside minority holders in distress.

rfm_tuples.R: Q3 FY24 10-Q (May 2024) Subsequent Events: 'On April 25, 2024, a subsidiary of the Company entered into a share purchase and transfer agreement to acquire the remaining equity interest in Holoplot GmbH not previously owned... Holoplot is now a consolidated subsidiary.'
rfm_tuples.f: Verify capital allocation discipline during going-concern period. Pre-cutoff capital actions add or alleviate distress?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Buyout of Holoplot (audio-tech vendor essential to Sphere's spatial sound) executed 20 days before cutoff, during going-concern period. Purchase price not disclosed in 10-Q (subsequent event, partial info). Company also issued $258.75M 3.50% Convertible Notes Dec 2023 and drew $65M on a delayed-draw term loan, indicating ongoing access to capital markets.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B finding: a distressed entity making strategic M&A (Holoplot) during a substantial-doubt quarter is either (a) confident in path to refinance, or (b) acquiring critical IP to protect Sphere asset value. Either reading argues AGAINST 'company is going BK' thesis. The $258M convert issuance at 3.50% (not distressed pricing) is further evidence that capital markets disagreed with a distress narrative at the SPHR holdco level.

insider_form4_summary.interpretation: Controlling-shareholder CEO net-buyer during going-concern quarter — strong contrarian-positive signal.

covenant_trajectory.interpretation: Tight, worsening — but no breach yet at cutoff.

cash_trajectory.interpretation: Recovered post-Sphere opening + convert issuance. Holdco solvency near-term not at risk.

segment_separation_logic.msgn_credit_facilities_security: non-recourse to Non-Credit Parties (Sphere, holdco, LV Sphere Term Loan)
segment_separation_logic.implication: An MSGN default would impair MSGN equity (the RSN business) but lenders' recourse limited to MSGN collateral. Holdco/Sphere could survive an MSGN default with subsidiary impairment but no cross-default to LV Sphere Term Loan or convertible notes.

summary: SPHR is a TWO-COMPANIES-IN-ONE situation: (1) MSG Networks — a structurally declining RSN with tightening covenants (5.36/5.50 leverage; 2.24/2.00 interest coverage at Q3 FY24) and explicit substantial-doubt going-concern language since Q1 FY24, driven by the Oct 2024 maturity of its credit facilities; (2) Sphere Las Vegas — a newly opened ($2.25B capex), revenue-generating venue ($170M Q3 rev) with non-recourse-to-MSGN debt and a controlling-shareholder CEO (James L. Dolan) making ~$10M of OPEN-MARKET PURCHASES at $40-48 in Feb-Mar 2024 AFTER going-concern disclosure. Disclosures are largely honest: Deloitte audit, no resignations, FY22 material weakness remediated, London cancellation impairment ($115.7M) was timely recognized. Findings: 1S/3M/2P/1U/1?. The framework's 'lying detector' returns mostly PASS/MODERATE — this is not an obscured-distress story; it is a transparently disclosed distressed segment cross-collateralized with a viable growth segment. Mode-B insider buying signal materially weakens a SHORT-tier thesis.
verdict_rationale: Genuine distress at MSGN subsidiary justifies the -25.7% drawdown — not over-discounted. But (a) non-recourse ring-fencing protects Sphere/holdco from MSGN default, (b) CEO open-market insider buying during going-concern period contradicts a SHORT-tier interpretation, (c) capital-markets access (Dec 2023 $258M convertible at 3.50%) was not distressed, (d) audit quality is strong. SHORT-tier requires the Sphere LV venue thesis to fail or holdco-level liquidity to deteriorate — neither is supported by pre-cutoff disclosure. LONG-tier requires Sphere LV to materially beat — possible but not provable from filings alone. NEUTRAL is the disciplined call.
